articles.summary: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) today announced it has reached a major wildfire safety milestone, installing and energizing 1,500 miles of underground power lines in high fire-threat districts since launching its undergrounding program in 2021. Wildfire ignition risk on the 1,500 miles of undergrounded lines is permanently reduced by approximately 98%. Customers served by underground lines also experience approximately 90% fewer outages. "Undergrounding is one of the most powerful tools we have to protect our customers and communities from wildfire risk. Reaching 1,500 miles is an important milestone, but what matters most is what those miles deliver: safer communities, fewer outages, and more reliable electric service over decades for the customers we're privileged to serve. We're proud of this progress and remain focused on doing this work where it can deliver the greatest safety and reliability benefits," said Matt Pender, PGE Undergrounding and System Hardening
articles.title: PG&E Achieves 1,500-Mile Milestone in Major Wildfire Safety Undergrounding Effort

articles.summary: Celebrating National STEM Day on Nov. 8 by Helping Students Pursue STEM Careers Link to B-roll video and soundbites of STEM recipients The PGE Corporation Foundation (PGE Foundation) awarded $327,500 in scholarships to dozens of students pursuing degrees in science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) at colleges and universities across California and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) nationwide. As communities celebrate National STEM Day on Nov. 8, the PGE Foundation reaffirms its commitment to building tomorrow's workforce through investments in STEM education and scholarships. This year, scholarships in the amounts of $2,500, $5,000 and $10,000 are being granted to 57 students from across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PGE) service area through the program. articles.summary: To help customers prepare their gas appliances for safe use during the cold weather months ahead, Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PGE) offers free in-home gas safety checks. During the gas safety checks, PGE also will re-light pilot lights for customers who have heaters or other appliances that have been turned off during warmer months. Free safety checks help ensure that gas appliances, including water heaters, furnaces and ovens, are operating safely and efficiently, reducing the risk of carbon monoxide (CO) poisoning within the home. Carbon monoxide is especially dangerous because it can't be seen, smelled or heard. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention , each year more than 400 Americans die from unintentional CO poisoning not linked to fires, more than 100,000 visit the emergency room, and more than 14,000 are hospitalized.
